exp1.name: False positives when nothing happened
exp1.detail: The real treated corners keep their real geography and their real comparison locations. Only the installation month is replaced, by a random month at least 48 months from the true one, so the analysis window contains no installation. A design with correct size rejects on 5 per cent of draws.

exp2.name: False positives under selection on a crash spike
exp2.detail: Untreated intersections are given random months, and the 143 of them with the highest pedestrian crash count inside a selection window become fake treated sites. Nothing is installed. The selection window is swept from the 12 months before installation out to the third year before it, because the real one is not published. Every rejection here is a false benefit, which is the direction policy acts on.

exp3.name: Power and size under selection on a persistent level
exp3.truth: a reduction of 20 per cent in the power pass, and no effect in the null pass
exp3.detail: The sites are the busiest 800 of the untreated pool over the whole record, and 143 are drawn per replication with independent random months, which reaches an exposure close to the real treated corners. The power pass thins every month of the after period at probability 0.8, which inserts a true reduction of 20 per cent. The null pass installs nothing.

size_correction_note: Power is also reported size corrected. A design that rejects too often under the null also finds a true effect more often, so comparing raw power would reward that fault. The size corrected figure takes the 95th percentile of each design's own null distribution of the test statistic from the first experiment as its critical value, and asks how often the power pass exceeds it.
two_regimes: Each design attains approximately the nominal rejection rate in one regime of site selection and rejects far too often in the other. A corridor comparison is correctly sized when selection acts on a persistent level and rejects on 34 to 88 per cent of null draws when it acts on a transient spike. A matched comparison is correctly sized when selection acts inside the months the matcher balances and rejects on 78 per cent of null draws when it acts on a persistent level. Each design's bias runs in the direction of the estimate it reports, so neither of the two published answers is evidence about the treatment until the mixture of transient and persistent in the city's selection is known. This repository cannot establish that mixture, because the city has published neither the list it selected from nor the vintage of the crash data it selected on.
